subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and any host/system filesystem browser scope, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the request changes which files operator clients can read or write and crosses a deliberate file-access boundary that current main only extends for read-only previews.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only Next Step
options.body: Keep system filesystem browsing out of scope and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded `agents.workspace.*` design with explicit read/admin scopes, path safety, limits, and UI proof.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap-Only Editing
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap and memory files while using read-only workspace previews for non-editable file inspection.

options.title: Open System Scope Design
options.body: Require a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit operator opt-in, auditing, read/write limits, and recovery UX before any implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only Next Step
recommendation.body: Keep system filesystem browsing out of scope and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded `agents.workspace.*` design with explicit read/admin scopes, path safety, limits, and UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace RPC slice and recent history ties them to the Gateway/mobile file-access product boundary.
